findings.title: QuantumFloat encoder rounds large binary-string integers
findings.description: A valid 54-bit basis input 2^53+1 with addend 0 silently produces 2^53 with probability 1. Upstream QuantumFloat.encoder divides through jnp.float64 before converting back to integer. The output decoder cannot restore lost input bits.
findings.resolution: Author replaced QuantumFloat.encoder initialization with per-bit X and replaced polynomial __iadd__ with public gidney_adder(Python int, register). Independently verified exact 54, 55, 65 and 80-bit cases including overflow, plus uniform superposition. No product file was edited by reviewer.

upstreamUnitCheck.observation: Installed QDK GateBased documentation explicitly defines gate_time, measurement_time and two_qubit_gate_time in ns; two-qubit time defaults to gate_time.

verifiedObservations: QURI Pauli index 0 is the leftmost output character; nonadjacent directed controls and asymmetric X/Y/Z observables agree with independent dense algebra. estimatorError=0 is correctly described only as absence of finite-shot sampling error.

QDK generated source preserves CZ operands and terminal ResetAll. Tripling all physical durations triples runtime while preserving physical qubits and modeled error. Default trace transformations, search space, SurfaceCode and RoundBasedFactory remain model assumptions, not hardware forecasts.

Qualtran arithmetic resource weights preserve an exact result larger than 2^53 via decimal-string serialization. Controlled-swap and zero-threshold comparison semantics agree with explicit checks. The 4-T default cost convention is not claimed as an ancilla-free unitary Toffoli decomposition.

OpenFermion complex non-Hermitian ordered ladder products agree elementwise with independently built occupation matrices for Jordan-Wigner and an explicit Fenwick parity basis transform for Bravyi-Kitaev; maximum matrix error 1.12e-16.
DDSIM coherent premeasurement state includes complex phase and Qiskit little-endian indexing; sampling-only output preserves q[n-1]...q[0] labels and omits dense state materialization.

QMAP initial/final maps and global phase reproduce all 16 logical basis columns on a five-wire directed topology, including idle logical wires and extra physical ancilla. Maximum unitary error 1.20e-15, ancillary leakage below 9e-16. Directed CX edges and undirected SWAP adjacency are valid; documented SWAP macro still needs hardware-basis lowering.
All numerical probe socket connections were denied. Skill/Tool declarations retain explicit dependency preparation, workspace-write side-effect classification and scientificValidation=not_evaluated.
